The full run reported 34 failed, 2594 passed, 24 skipped and 1 xfailed. Seven test files contain failing tests:

| File | Failures |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_arguments.py` | 1 (`test_nargs_star`) |
| `tests/test_basic.py` | 1 (`test_basic_functionality`) |
| `tests/test_commands.py` | 1 (`test_other_command_invoke`) |
| `tests/test_context.py` | 1 (`test_ensure_context_objects`) |
| `tests/test_options.py` | 1 (`test_prefixes`) |
| `tests/test_parser.py` | 5 (`test_split_arg_string[...]`) |
| `tests/test_utils/test_echo_via_pager.py` | 24 (`test_echo_via_pager[...]`) |

- **The output was truncated.** The console summary showed only 10 of the 34 failures, and those covered the first six files. I got the other 24, all in `test_echo_via_pager.py`, by recalling the full saved output of that same run, so I didn't re-run the suite.
- **`tests/test_chain.py::test_group_chaining`** is an expected failure (xfail), not a real failure, so I left it out.
- **Six of these files have uncommitted modifications** in git status: every file in the table except `test_echo_via_pager.py`. In the first five, the failing assertions look inverted: `assert not result.exception` fails even though the result is `<Result okay>`. In `test_parser.py`, the failures show `assert not [...] == [...]`, so the comparisons are also negated. I didn't change anything.
- **The pager failures are a different kind.** In `test_echo_via_pager.py` the captured pager output is empty (`'' == 'testtest\n'`). That file has no uncommitted changes, so this may be an environment problem, such as `less` not being available. I haven't confirmed the cause.
